value: Study used explorative shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal specimens from Swedish students before and after travel to the Indian peninsula or Central Africa.

extraction_warnings: This paper reports aggregate/study-level demographic and clinical statistics (ranges, medians, percentages) rather than per-subject or per-sample rows; individual subject_id/sample_id data likely reside only in supplementary Table S1, which is not included in the provided text.

Some variables (e.g., diarrhea incidence, malaria prophylaxis use, ESBL acquisition) are stratified by travel destination (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) but these specific variables are not part of the provided schema fields, so subgroup-level detail is only noted for 'subcohort'.
Sex is reported only as an aggregate percentage (74% female) across the whole mixed-sex cohort; no single categorical value was extracted for the enum field.

This paper concerns gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance gene changes in healthy travelers, not oncologic, neonatal, obstetric, or FMT studies; most schema fields are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

Biomarker fields were populated using the three most prominently reported fold-change values (sulfonamide, trimethoprim, beta-lactam resistance genes) from the abstract/results; additional granular biomarker data (e.g., absolute resistance gene counts per 16S rRNA for tetracycline and aminoglycoside genes) exist in Table 1 but were not extracted to avoid overfitting the biomarker list beyond the schema's intended scope.
No explicit 'Healthy' disease status statement was found verbatim, so disease_details was left as not_reported despite the study population being ostensibly healthy volunteers.
No canonical study_name was explicitly provided in the text; field marked not_reported.
DNA extraction kit details likely reside in supplemental material not included in provided text.

Two sequencing platforms (Illumina HiSeq 2000 for metagenomics, Illumina MiSeq for isolate genomes) were used; schema allows only one enum value, so HiSeq was chosen as primary platform for the main metagenomic analysis.
target_condition field interpreted broadly as antibiotic resistance gene dissemination/ESBL acquisition since no classical disease condition was studied.
